title: Threat model, data-protection design, compliance mapping and security overview
story: As a carrier security reviewer I want a STRIDE threat model, data-protection design and compliance mapping tied to concrete code controls so that I can assess the platform for licensing.
acceptance: architecture/threat-model.md contains a mermaid trust-boundary diagram covering browser/client, API/router, modules, SQLite store, outbox/webhooks, AI provider, mock PAS and file storage

STRIDE table has one row set per component and per trust boundary of architecture/overview.md, each with threat, mitigation and a control citing a real src/core file (auth.mjs, store.mjs, crypto.mjs, audit.mjs, bus.mjs, log.mjs, router.mjs, tenant-context.mjs); reviewer greps cited files exist
Top-10 risks ranked by likelihood x impact with mitigation, owner team and status (implemented/planned)

Multi-tenant isolation section analyses store rewriting limits (regex SQL rewrite, CTE/string-literal gaps from core-runtime-api.md assumptions), X-Tenant-Id handling, per-tenant keys, tctx binding and cache, with residual risks

AI-specific section covers prompt injection via uploaded documents, untrusted model output (schema validation, confidence/explanation, human review), data sent to providers (minimization, redaction, no-training terms, per-tenant opt-out) and provider failure

architecture/data-protection.md has a PII inventory table generated from x-pii fields in architecture/contracts/domain/*.schema.json (field, schema, handling), encryption at rest per tenant key via ctx.crypto.encryptPii/hmacIndex, key-management and rotation path to Cloud KMS, retention schedule, log redaction rules (ctx.log key list), and the synthetic-data-only rule

docs/compliance-mapping.md has tables mapping GLBA Safeguards Rule, NAIC #668, state claim-handling timelines (WI/IL/MI marked illustrative, how claims timers implement acknowledge/decide/pay deadlines) and SOC 2 CC6, CC7, CC8 to control -> evidence location (file or test path)
docs/security-overview.md is a customer-facing summary (<=2 pages) with no internal-only detail, no real carrier names, and links to the other docs; claims not yet built are labelled planned
No secrets, real names or real carriers anywhere; only the four owned paths changed
brief: Read architecture/overview.md first and enumerate its components and trust boundaries; build the STRIDE tables from that list so nothing is missed. Then read src/core/*.mjs and cite real behavior only: do not claim controls that are not in code. Mark gaps as 'planned' with an owning team. Known facts to use: tokens are HMAC-SHA256 dev tokens (auth.mjs) with key derived from master key; /api/v1/auth/token is dev-mode only; X-Tenant-Id only for platform_admin; store.forTenant rewrites SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE with a tenant filter, raw INSERT into tenant tables throws, system store throws on tenant tables; crypto derives per-tenant keys (deriveKey), encryptPii/decryptPii/hmacIndex; audit_log is hash-chained and append-only via triggers, verify() available, GET /api/v1/audit needs supervisor/carrier_admin/platform_admin; events carry no PII (ids/codes/scores) and webhooks are HMAC-SHA256 signed; logger redacts keys matching name|email|phone|dob|address|ssn|license|plate; 15MB body limit. Grep x-pii in architecture/contracts/domain/ for the PII inventory (script it if many; keep output in the table). Timers: claims module owns regulatory timers per architecture/overview.md decisions; describe the mechanism generically and label WI/IL/MI day counts illustrative (not legal advice). Evidence location column should point to tests/security/*.test.mjs (written by S1-SEC-02) where applicable. Key rotation: describe versioned key ids, re-encrypt job, KMS envelope encryption (data key wrapped by Cloud KMS key per tenant) as the path; mark as planned. Include a short residual-risk/backlog list for Sprint 2. Use mermaid fenced blocks. Do not edit src/ or tests/. Post any contract gap to the architecture hub.
requirements: Threat model per component and trust boundary
GLBA, NAIC 668, state timelines, SOC 2 mapping

verdicts.reason: All four docs meet criteria (mermaid + STRIDE for 13 components/9 boundaries, ranked top-10, isolation limits R1/R3/R4 reproduced by me, AI threats, PII inventory 14/7 matches x-pii, GLBA/NAIC/SOC2/state timelines illustrative, planned items labelled); nit: a few src line cites are off (e.g. bus.mjs:163 is really ~56)
